checks.title: APP_DEBUG is false and APP_ENV is production
checks.why: With debug on, Laravel's error page prints the stack trace, the resolved config and every environment variable, including database and mail credentials, to whoever triggered the error.
checks.action: Set APP_ENV to production and APP_DEBUG to false in the production environment, then confirm no deploy step overwrites them.

verify.expect: APP_ENV is production and APP_DEBUG is false. If nothing prints, confirm both are set in the host environment.

checks.title: APP_KEY is set to a generated value
checks.why: APP_KEY encrypts sessions and signed URLs. An empty key breaks encryption outright, and a key copied from a public skeleton or tutorial lets anyone forge a session cookie for your application.
checks.action: Generate a unique key for the production environment and store it as a secret. Rotating it invalidates existing sessions and any encrypted column, so plan it deliberately.

verify.expect: A non-empty base64 value that is unique to this deployment and not shared with any other environment.

checks.title: Config, routes, views and events are cached in production
checks.why: Without the caches, every request re-parses every config file and re-registers every route. On a medium application this is routinely the largest fixed cost in the request, before any of your code runs.
checks.action: Run the config, route, view and event cache commands as part of the deploy, after the code is in place and before traffic is switched over.

verify.expect: The cache files exist. If they do not, confirm the deploy script generates them rather than relying on the first request.

checks.title: The queue connection is not sync in production
checks.why: The sync driver runs every queued job inside the request that dispatched it, so a queued email or export blocks the user and ties response time to a third party you do not control.
checks.action: Point QUEUE_CONNECTION at a real driver such as redis or database, and run a supervised worker process alongside the application.

verify.expect: A real queue driver rather than sync. If nothing prints, the framework default applies and should be set explicitly.

checks.title: Session cookies are marked secure and http-only
checks.why: Without the secure flag the session cookie is sent over any plaintext request, and without http-only any cross-site scripting flaw upgrades directly into full session theft.
checks.action: Set SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE to true, leave http-only enabled, and set SESSION_SAME_SITE to lax or strict for the flows your application supports.

verify.expect: SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE is true, and SESSION_SAME_SITE is lax or strict.

checks.title: Telescope, Debugbar and Ignition are not installed in production
checks.why: Telescope records every request, query and job payload behind a route that is easy to leave unprotected. Ignition has previously carried a remote code execution flaw reachable whenever debug mode is on.
checks.action: Require these packages under require-dev only, and confirm the production install omits dev dependencies so their service providers never register.

verify.expect: Nothing is printed. Any match means a debug package is present in the production dependency set.

checks.title: The public storage symlink exists
checks.why: Without the symlink every user upload served from public storage returns a 404. The failure is silent at deploy time and only shows up when someone loads a page with an uploaded image on it.
checks.action: Create the storage symlink as part of the deploy, and make sure the deploy is repeatable if the release directory is replaced each time.

verify.expect: A symlink pointing at the storage app public directory.

checks.title: The production log level is not debug
checks.why: At debug level Laravel logs full query bindings and request payloads, which fills the disk quickly and writes user data, tokens and password reset values into plaintext log files.
checks.action: Set LOG_LEVEL to warning or error in production, use a channel with rotation, and ship logs somewhere with retention rules rather than leaving them on disk.

verify.expect: LOG_LEVEL is warning or stricter, and LOG_CHANNEL points at a rotating or forwarded channel rather than a single file.

checks.title: The reported environment summary matches what you intended to deploy
checks.why: Laravel resolves configuration from several layers, and a cached config file built in the wrong environment will keep serving stale values that no environment file explains.
checks.action: Have the operator print the framework's own environment summary on the deployed host and compare the environment, debug flag, cache drivers and queue connection against what was intended.

verify.expect: Environment is production, debug is off, and the cache, session and queue drivers match the infrastructure you actually run.

checks.title: Destructive migrations have been reviewed before release
checks.why: A migration that drops or renames a column is irreversible in practice once traffic resumes, and rolling back the application code will not bring the data back. How much ceremony this deserves depends on your data.
checks.action: Consider reviewing the pending migrations for column drops and renames, and splitting them into an additive release followed by a cleanup release once nothing reads the old shape.
